Addis Ababa, the capital of Ethiopia, was founded in 1886 by Emperor Menelik II and Empress Taytu at hot springs below the Entoto hills; its name means new flower.

Menelik moved his court down from Entoto, and the town grew around the palace. Fast-growing eucalyptus trees brought from Australia saved it from running out of firewood. The railway from Djibouti reached it in 1917.

It became the seat of the Organisation of African Unity in 1963, now the African Union, and of the UN Economic Commission for Africa, so that it is often called the political capital of Africa. Today it is one of the largest cities on the continent.
sum: Addis Ababa, the capital of Ethiopia, was founded in 1886 by Emperor Menelik II and Empress Taytu at hot springs below the Entoto hills; its name means new flower.
